newsitem.title: OMAN: Gulf states concerned about violence, "extremism".
newsitem.headline: Gulf states concerned about violence, "extremism".

text.p: Gulf countries are seriously concerned about violence and "extremism" in the region and are focusing on the issues during an interior ministers' meeting on Monday, a senior Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) official said.

Interior ministers of the GCC, meeting in the Omani capital, were giving "special attention to the subject of violence, terrorism and extremism", the GCC's Assistant Secretary-General Abdelaziz Bu Ali told reporters.

"The GCC countries are very concerned with these subjects and there is a trend among GCC leaders to ensure this subject receives the attention it deserves for the stability and security of the GCC states," he said.
"(The issues are) directly related to the development and flourishing of states in the region," he added.
Bu Ali said the interior ministers were discussing a number of security issues, and their findings would be submitted to GCC leaders at their summit in Qatar next month.
The GCC is a political, economic and military alliance which groups Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman.
In Bahrain, at least 27 people have been killed since anti-government protests by members of the Shi'ite Moslem community broke out in December 1994.
Security concerns in Saudi Arabia have increased after two bombings against U.S. targets in the kingdom which killed 24 Americans and two Indians since November, 1995.
